figures.finding: Where a written law permits a person under eighteen to be employed, the employer must ensure a parent's consent has been obtained and produce evidence of it on an authorised officer's request; no Nauruan Act sets a minor's contractual capacity or a set-aside of earnings.

value.employment: parent's consent, kept by the employer (Child Protection and Welfare Act 2016 s. 53(2))

figures.applies: Reaches any employment of a child, so a writer or director as well as a performer; contracts outside employment fall to the common law adopted by the Custom and Adopted Laws Act 1971 (not read).

sources.said: Where a child has been employed by reason of any written law which permits the employment of a person who is under 18 years of age, it is the responsibility of the employer to ensure that the consent of a parent has been obtained, and the employer shall produce evidence of such consent if requested to do so by an authorised officer.

figures.finding: A person under eighteen cannot be a director of a Nauruan corporation.
figures.applies: From the prescribed consent form (Form 3 of the Corporations (Forms and Fees) Regulations 2018, printed with the Act); the section of the Act it reflects wasn't located in the text.

sources.said: A person cannot be a director of a corporation if he or she is any of the following: (a) under 18 years of age;
